history.sg_progress: The Administration wishes to note that the performance of heads of entities for achieving key performance indicators on geographical representation is continuously monitored as part of the Geographical Diversity Strategy through meetings between the Under-Secretary-General for Management Strategy, Policy and Compliance and each head of entity to highlight the importance of the equitable geographical representation and gender parity imperatives and to discuss : (a) the entities’ action plans; (b) possible scenarios and outcomes; and (c) the way forward and next steps for accelerating the progress. Furthermore, in the first and second quarters of 2022, the Office of Human Resources conducted meetings with the entities at the director level to emphasize the importance of their role as hiring managers in making selection recommendations to their heads of entities, taking into account the targets for geographical representation and gender parity under the senior management compact with the Secretary-General. During the meetings, scorecards showing the targets and actual performance were presented, along with details of how entities could regularly monitor their progress through the accountability indicator monitoring module of the management dashboard. The Administration considers this recommendation to have been implemented and requests its closure by the Board.

In addition, the network was set up in 2022 to support entities with capacity- building and knowledge-sharing on best practices on talent outreach, sourcing and acquisition and advancing equitable geographical distribution.

history.sg_progress: The Administration monitors the performance of heads of entities against the equitable geographical distribution target in the senior manager’s compact. In addition, in July 2023 the Office of Human Resources established a Management Client Board working group with entity representatives to revise further the geographical diversity strategy, monitor the key performance indicator on geographical representation for each entity, provide guidance to entities on targeted talent outreach and proactively establish measures and actions to improve geographical representation. Furthermore, in August 2023 the Office launched a package to assist with career outreach, which provides a multitude of resources, including information on best practices and guidelines, branded templates, materials for career events, an image library, frequently asked questions and talent outreach channels. This package has been shared with all entities. The Office also continues to make enhancements to its global talent pool to support entities by allowing them to tap into unrepresented and underrepresented talent. The network to support and multiply talent outreach, facilitated by the Office of Human Resources, holds regular meetings and continues to be an important forum for the sharing of best practices on talent outreach among entities. The Administration considers this recommendation to be implemented and requests its closure by the Board.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration continue to monitor the performance of heads of entities for achieving key performance indicators on geographical representation, issue guidance to entities and develop more proactive measures to improve geographical representation.
history.administration_response: The Office of Human Resources has continued to monitor entities’ performance regarding geographical representation, has issued guidance and worked in proactive measure to improve geographical representation. Entities, including special political missions and peacekeeping operations, have established focal points on equitable geographical distribution and the Office is working with the focal points to share information on progress for entities whose representation status is shared in the monthly communication on equitable geographical distribution. In January 2024, the Office gave a presentation to the heads of entities at the Management Committee meeting on the importance of and progress in equitable geographical distribution, changes to the system of desirable ranges through General Assembly resolution 77/278 and their impact on equitable geographical distribution, and a new approach to improving equitable geographical distribution. In February 2024, the Office again gave a presentation to the heads of entities through the Management Client Board, underlining their pivotal role in accelerating progress towards equitable geographical distribution and prioritizing the attainment of the targets. In April 2024, the Assistant Secretary-General of the Office of Human Resources will be sending a communication to heads of entities emphasizing the urgency of bringing every Member State within its desirable range. As we have issued guidance to entities and undertaken actions to work out more proactive measures to improve geographical representation, we consider the recommendation closed.
history.board_assessment: Given that the auditors found that some similar issues still exist in the 2023 final audit, the Board considers this recommendation to be under implementation.

history.entities_raw: Department of Management Strategy, Policy and Compliance
history.sg_progress: The Administration has continued to monitor entities’ performance regarding geographical representation, issued guidance and worked on proactive measures to improve equitable geographical distribution for geographical posts and greater geographical representation for non-geographical posts. In April 2024, a communication from the Assistant Secretary-General for Human Resources was dispatched to all heads of entities sharing each entity’s performance data towards the equitable geographical distribution target from 2020 to In the communication, the urgency of making progress was reiterated, especially in the light of General Assembly resolution 77/278, by which the Assembly expanded the posts subject to the system of desirable ranges to include all posts funded by the regular budget at the Professional and higher categories. This includes special political missions and peacekeeping operations, but excludes language posts. The heads of entities were also reminded of the General Assembly’s request to urge senior managers to meet the geographical targets outlined in their compacts. In addition, they were informed of the requirement to report on progress achieved in the report on the composition of the Secretariat during the seventy-ninth session of the Assembly. As part of efforts to improve equitable geographical distribution for geographical posts, the Office of Human Resources continues to conduct targeted talent outreach and purposeful partnerships with Member States and resident coordinators and the United Nations information centres and overhaul the staff selection process, which is more of a long-term measure. The Administration considers this recommendation to be implemented and requests its closure by the Board.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration continue to monitor the performance of heads of entities for achieving key performance indicators on geographical representation, issue guidance to entities and develop more proactive measures to improve geographical representation.
history.administration_response: The Administration considers this recommendation to be implemented. The objective of the recommendation was for the Administration to continue to monitor the performance of heads of entities under key performance indicators relating to geographical distribution, issue guidance to entities and implement more proactive measures to improve geographical distribution. The Administration demonstrated that it had conducted outreach activities to increase the pool of eligible applicants from unrepresented and underrepresented Member States, provided continuous guidance and support to heads of entities, established monitoring of key performance indicators through management dashboards, included a “geographical appointments” indicator in senior manager’s compacts and reported on geographical distribution in the report of the Secretary-General on the composition of the Secretariat: staff demographics. However, the hiring restrictions imposed owing to the Organization’s financial crisis in the past few years has affected the achievement of geographical distribution. Therefore, it is not necessary to keep this recommendation open, given the Administration’s efforts to continuously improve the monitoring of and reporting on geographical distribution.
history.board_assessment: Given the Administration’s concerted and sustained efforts to enhance geographical representation, including through the special measures being carried out, the Board considers this recommendation to be implemented.
